questions.q: What does a tool's "description" field actually do?
options: It's purely cosmetic documentation the API ignores
It must exactly match the tool's "name" field
The model reads it to decide when the tool is relevant to call
It sets the tool's maximum execution time
questions.explain: The description is what the model actually reads when deciding whether and when to call a tool — it should read like real documentation.

questions.q: What syntax does a tool's input_schema use to describe its arguments?
options: Real JSON Schema (type, properties, required)
A proprietary Anthropic-only syntax unrelated to JSON Schema
Plain English only
XML
questions.explain: input_schema reuses standard JSON Schema — the same type/properties/required structure covered in Chapter 2.

questions.q: When Claude wants to call a tool, what does it actually do?
options: It directly executes the function in Anthropic's infrastructure
It silently fails and returns no content
It returns a tool_use content block naming the tool and its input — your code runs it
It emails the developer the function to run
questions.explain: For a client tool, Claude never executes code itself — it returns a structured tool_use block, and your application runs the actual operation.

questions.q: What field links a tool_result back to the specific tool_use call it answers?
options: name
input_schema
description
tool_use_id
questions.explain: tool_result includes tool_use_id, matching the id Claude generated in its original tool_use block.

questions.q: Why does the Messages API's content field need to be an array of blocks rather than a single string?
options: So a response can mix text and tool_use blocks in one reply
Arrays are required by the HTTP spec
It's purely a historical quirk with no use today
Strings aren't valid JSON values
questions.explain: An array lets one response carry multiple content types together — exactly what's needed when a reply includes both explanatory text and a tool call.
